messages:
daria: Quick proposal — we should add a short, stable client-facing status header (X-RW-Status) separate from HTTP codes so clients can make routing/UX decisions without parsing body text. Thinking values: ok, degraded, fallback, quota_block, rate_limited, internal_error.
kevin: +1 to a stable header, but we need to avoid coupling to internal routing labels. Can we map runtime variants to a small public enum instead?
matt: agree with kev. Also want to ensure telemetry emits both raw route and public status for SLO dashboards. If we expose X-RW-Status we should sample route-level traces for non-ok statuses.
julie: product POV: console should show per-route badging (green/amber/red) based on public status distribution. If we change header semantics later it'll break customers — need versioning.
daria: proposal v1: 6 public statuses (ok, degraded, fallback, quota, throttled, error) + header X-RW-Status-V=1. Keep internal route id in telemetry only (no client exposure).
kevin: how do we map 429/503/5xx? Example mapping: 429 => throttled, 503 failover to fallback or error depending on fallback success, 5xx => error. 409/422 map to client_error (not in this list).
sam_devex: important: SDKs should translate X-RW-Status into well-documented enums and surfaced via SDK exceptions or helper helpers. Devex can push a changelog and small migration guide.
matt: telemetry detail: emit metric rw_status_count{status=v, route=ROUTE_HASH} and a sample field for route_version so we can correlate regressions after rollouts. Also emit a breadcrumb with trace id when status != ok.
daria: rollout plan: start internal only (console flag + header returned only for orgs on beta) for 2 weeks, collect telemetry, then public opt-in for SDKs, then opt-out deprecation cycle. Can we gate on tenant tier?
julie: yep, start with enterprise tenants and a few PLG partners. UX note: console badges should be per-route and a daily histogram. Add a tooltip that explains statuses and recommended remediation.
kevin: edge-case: when we route to cheaper quantized model fallback, should we return 'fallback' or try to keep 'ok' and add a quality_hint header? I prefer explicit 'fallback' so clients can show subtle degraded UX.
matt: fallback + quality_hint makes sense. quality_hint numeric 0-1 could help client autoscaling decisions. But stringify to keep header simple, e.g., X-RW-Quality: low|med|high.
sam_devex: plus docs snippet and example: ```js // SDK sample const resp = await client.generate(...) console.log(resp.headers['x-rw-status']); if (resp.headers['x-rw-status']=='fallback') showADegradedBadge(); ```
deploy-bot: deploy queued: feature-flag x-rw-status header (runtime flag) -> env: eng-platform-beta, expected deploy: 10m. :rocket:
ops-bot: note: ensure the CDN and proxies (nginx / gp-proxy) pass through and normalize header casing. Add test in infra CI to validate header pass-through.
daria: action items: 1) kevin/matt: draft mapping table from HTTP codes + routing outcome -> X-RW-Status + quality header (due EOD). 2) sam_devex: SDK docs + example (due +3d). 3) julie: console mockups for badges and tooltip (due +5d). 4) infra: add pass-through test (matt). I'll create a tracking ticket and a canary flag.
kevin: tiny nit — use X-RW-Status not X-RW-State. Status reads better with existing headers.
daria: noted. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
